headline: SwarmEvolve reports faster program search with latent agent swarms
summary: Jiang and Karniadakis introduce SwarmEvolve, which runs 10 swarms of 45 Qwen3 agents that reason for 40 steps in latent space, select diverse traces and pass their KV caches to a summarizer that proposes programs. On 21 evaluator-driven mathematics and scientific-computing tasks, the authors report the highest average score against OpenEvolve, ShinkaEvolve and CodeEvolve across Qwen3 8B, 14B and 32B-FP8, using three seeds and one GPU plus eight CPU cores per model setup. With Qwen3 8B they report improving three AlphaEvolve constructions. These are paper-reported results, not independently reproduced here. The experiments are limited to the selected tasks and compute regime; the linked GitHub repository is now accessible and contains benchmark tasks, evaluators, baselines and analysis, but its README says the core SwarmEvolve code is coming soon; the method still cannot be independently run from that repository.
